hints: Focus on what each test is really telling you, one test rules out easily oxidised groups and the other rules out carbonyl groups.
No colour change with acidified dichromate(VI) means X is not a primary alcohol, secondary alcohol or aldehyde, so think about what type of alcohol is resistant to oxidation.
A negative 2,4-DNPH test means no aldehyde or ketone is present, so combine both clues to pick the compound that is neither oxidisable nor a carbonyl.
walkthrough:
**Interpret the dichromate test**

Think of acidified potassium dichromate(VI) as an oxidising agent that changes colour when it does its job. Orange $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ turns green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ when it oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde or acid, a secondary alcohol to a ketone, or an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.

No colour change means: $$\text{no oxidation occurs}$$

**Interpret the 2,4-DNPH test**

Remember 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine is the classic test for a carbonyl group. Aldehydes and ketones give a yellow-orange precipitate, while alcohols do not react at all.

No orange precipitate means: $$\text{no } \text{C=O} \text{ in an aldehyde or ketone}$$

**Combine the clues and check the options**

Put the two results together. X cannot be oxidised and it is not a carbonyl compound. That fits perfectly with a tertiary alcohol, which has no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the $\text{-OH}$ group and so resists oxidation.

Methylpropan-2-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, is a tertiary alcohol, so it gives both negative results.

options.A: Incorrect. Butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol. It is oxidised by warm acidified dichromate(VI) to butan-2-one, so orange to green colour change would be seen.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde. It is oxidised to ethanoic acid (dichromate turns green) and it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It fails both observations.
options.C: Correct. Methylpropan-2-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, is a tertiary alcohol. It cannot be oxidised by dilute acidified dichromate(VI) so no colour change occurs, and with no $\text{C=O}$ group it gives no precipitate with 2,4-DNPH.
options.D: Incorrect. Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone. Although it resists oxidation so dichromate stays orange, it contains a carbonyl group and so gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH.
